Both the Unitree G1 and the Booster K1 are compact, highly capable humanoid robots designed for research, education, and AI development, but they target slightly different form factors and performance tiers.

Core Specifications Comparison

Feature
Unitree G1
Booster K1
Height
~127 cm (approx. 4.2 ft)
~95 cm (approx. 3.1 ft)
Weight
~35 kg
~19.5 kg
Degrees of Freedom (DoF)
23 (standard) up to 43+
22 (Head: 2, Arms: 4×2, Legs: 6×2)
Knee Torque
~90 N·m (standard) / up to 120 N·m
60 N·m
Perception Suite
Livox MID360 3D LiDAR + Depth Camera (e.g., RealSense D435i)
Wide-angle stereo/depth camera + 9-axis IMU
AI Computing
8-core CPU (Optional Jetson Orin modules in EDU versions)
Scalable options: 48, 117, or up to 200 TOPS (Qualcomm or Jetson Orin NX/AGX)
Battery Life
~2 hours
~30 mins (2Ah) to ~80 mins (5Ah)

Key Differences

Size and Portability:

The Booster K1 is smaller and lighter (95 cm, 19.5 kg), making it exceptionally portable, desktop-friendly, and easy to transport in a case between classrooms or labs.

The Unitree G1 is taller and heavier (~1.27 m, 35 kg), aligning closer to a miniature adult human profile with higher torque capacity and more robust physical presence.

Sensors and Navigation:

Unitree equips the G1 with a Livox MID360 3D LiDAR alongside depth cameras, giving it heavy-duty mapping and spatial awareness suited for complex environment navigation.

The K1 relies on a robust stereo/depth vision system and a 9-axis IMU, optimized for standard indoor research, lab environments, and platform competitions like RoboCup.

Actuation and Dexterity:

The G1 offers higher joint flexibility options (up to 43 DoF variants) and advanced hand configurations (including three-finger or five-finger dexterous hands).

The K1 features a balanced 22 DoF setup with torque-controlled smart servos designed for stable bipedal walking and foundational locomotion research.

Both the **Unitree G1** and the **Booster K1** are compact, highly capable humanoid robots designed for research, education, and AI development, but they target slightly different form factors and performance tiers. ### Core Specifications Comparison

| Feature | Unitree G1 | Booster K1 |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Height** |  ~127 cm (approx. 4.2 ft) | ~95 cm (approx. 3.1 ft) |
| **Weight** |  ~35 kg | ~19.5 kg |
| **Degrees of Freedom (DoF)** |  23 (standard) up to 43+ | 22 (Head: 2, Arms: 4×2, Legs: 6×2) |
| **Knee Torque** |  ~90 N·m (standard) / up to 120 N·m | 60 N·m |
| **Perception Suite** |  Livox MID360 3D LiDAR + Depth Camera (e.g., RealSense D435i) | Wide-angle stereo/depth camera + 9-axis IMU |
| **AI Computing** |  8-core CPU (Optional Jetson Orin modules in EDU versions) | Scalable options: 48, 117, or up to 200 TOPS (Qualcomm or Jetson Orin NX/AGX) |
| **Battery Life** |  ~2 hours | ~30 mins (2Ah) to ~80 mins (5Ah) |

### Key Differences

  * **Size and Portability:**

 * The **Booster K1** is smaller and lighter (95 cm, 19.5 kg), making it exceptionally portable, desktop-friendly, and easy to transport in a case between classrooms or labs.  * The K1 relies on a robust stereo/depth vision system and a 9-axis IMU, optimized for standard indoor research, lab environments, and platform competitions like RoboCup.   * **Actuation and Dexterity:**

 * The G1 offers higher joint flexibility options (up to 43 DoF variants) and advanced hand configurations (including three-finger or five-finger dexterous hands). [Unitree G1](https://www.unitree.com/g1#:~:text=About%2035kg%2B%20*%20Total%20Degrees%20of%20Freedom%EF%BC%88Joint,thumb%20has%203%20active%20degrees%20of%20freedom%3B)

 * The K1 features a balanced 22 DoF setup with torque-controlled smart servos designed for stable bipedal walking and foundational locomotion research.
